citation.wording: If you received rental income from real estate (including personal property leased with real estate), report the income on line 3. Use a separate column (A, B, or C) for each rental property. Include income received for renting a room or other space. Any other income should be included and reported on line 3, with a statement attached to your return.

sources.note: HOLD, not `sum_parts`, and this is the one line where they differ. Rent a tenant pays directly is reported by no information return at all, and a property manager's 1099-MISC box 1 covers only what the MANAGER collected — so a 1099 is a floor that can be far below the truth, and stating it as the year's rent understates the property with every total footing. `Any other income should be included` is the instruction's own way of saying the form is not the measure.

sources.note: `sum_parts` where rent holds, because the instruction names the form as the measure — *report this amount on line 4* — and a royalty has a payer who must report it, where a tenant has not. The figure summed is the GROSS: severance tax and depletion are deductions taken further down, not reasons to report less than box 2.

citation.wording: If you paid $600 or more in interest on a mortgage during 2025, the recipient should send you a Form 1098 or similar statement by January 31, 2026, showing the total interest received from you. If you paid more mortgage interest than is shown on your Form 1098 or similar statement, see Pub. 334 regarding deduction limits to find out if you can deduct part or all of the additional interest.

sources.note: THE INSTRUCTION ANTICIPATES BOTH SIDES OF THE CHECK. The 1098 shows *the total interest received from you*, so it is a part of the client's own figure — and the paragraph then contemplates the client having paid MORE than the form shows, which is the check holding rather than failing. Two loans on one property are two Forms 1098 and one record line; summing all three states the interest nearly twice.

form.client_item_note: `schedule_c_equivalent` is the Schedule C line a client's item goes to instead when the activity's `rent_character` is `significant_services` or `personal_property_business` — a bed-and-breakfast or an equipment-hire business is a TRADE, and its income and costs belong on Schedule C with self-employment tax, not on Schedule E without it. `null` on line 4 (royalties) because a royalty is not a rental and its own character fork is declared on the 1099-MISC. Two Schedule E lines map onto one Schedule C line — 8 and 11 both to commissions and fees, 7 and 14 both to repairs and maintenance — because Schedule C draws the line in fewer places; that is the form's own doing, not a collision.

paths.note:
WHERE A PART I FIGURE GOES, which is not what the face prints (research R3). Lines 24, 25 and 26 are all true of the form and none of them is a path: one expense on line 21 reaches line 26 through 24 as a subtraction AND through 25 as a subtraction of a subtraction, which is an addition — so the walk found two chains carrying opposite signs and `_more_direct` kept one by sorting hop ids. The sign of a real figure decided by which route id sorted first.

Which of the two a figure actually takes turns on whether the PROPERTY is a gain or a loss, and that is a fact about the activity's sum. So the printed arithmetic is marked `walk: false` and evaluated per activity by the ledger, and this one edge carries the figure: every Part I figure reaches line 26 once, by one chain, with one sign.

LINE 22 IS ON THE PATH TOO, and SUBTRACTS. It is *'Deductible rental real estate loss after limitation, if any, on Form 8582'* — a loss, printed as a positive magnitude, which line 25 adds to the losses and line 26 then takes away. Left off the path it reached the face by nothing at all: it fed only line 25, and line 25 is presentation. A figure allowed by the passive limitation, absent from the return.
